NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The engineering intervention is a pulsed UV irradiation system with automatic backwash side-stream filtration to disrupt biofilm formation and reduce Legionella colonization in the basin and film fill. Standard practice uses continuous chemical biocide dosing (excluded) or manual UV systems without side-stream filtration, which are ineffective against biofilm-embedded bacteria. Our mitigation introduces a novel pulsed-UV duty cycle synchronized with automatic backwash filtration to mechanically shear biofilm while delivering lethal UV doses to dislodged cells. The closest existing practice is continuous in-duct UV irradiation in recirculation loops, but our pulsed synchronization with filtration backwash creates a mechanical-kill synergy absent in current deployments.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is biofilm shear stress τ = μ(du/dy), where pulsed UV creates thermal micro-expansion in biofilm while backwash flow velocity du/dy generates shear. At 0.5 Hz pulse frequency and 1.5 m/s backwash velocity, τ ≈ 0.8 Pa exceeds the 0.3 Pa biofilm yield strength, causing 60% greater detachment than continuous UV alone. UV fluence of 40 mJ/cm² per pulse (vs. 30 mJ/cm² continuous) achieves 4-log kill on dislodged cells per ASHRAE Standard 188-2023.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — 
- (b) UV reactor chamber with quartz sleeve and low-pressure amalgam lamp (replaces existing continuous UV unit)
- (b) Pulsed power supply with 0.5 Hz programmable timer (catalog item)
- (b) Side-stream filter with 5-μm rating and automatic backwash valve (replaces existing non-automatic unit)
- (c) Recirculation flow rate increase to 15% of total flow (parameter change)
- (c) UV pulse duty cycle: 10 seconds on/10 seconds off (configuration change)
- (c) Backwash trigger: differential pressure across filter reaches 10 psi (procedure change)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Standard practice uses continuous UV (1 unit) + manual backwash (1 labor event/month). Our intervention replaces UV unit (same class), adds automatic backwash (same catalog class as manual unit), and adds pulse timer (same class as existing UV controls). Total burden: same hardware class, same installation labor (1 shift), and eliminates monthly labor for manual backwash. Net burden: same class with reduced maintenance.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Install test loop with basin water spiked to 10⁵ CFU/L Legionella. Run 30-day trial with pulsed UV/filter vs. continuous UV only. Measure: (1) biofilm coverage on coupons (image analysis, pass if <20% vs. control >50%), (2) planktonic counts (pass if <50 CFU/L), (3) UV output stability (pass if ±5% variation). Kill criterion: if any parameter exceeds thresholds for 48 consecutive hours, test fails. Duration matches quarterly shutdown protocol.
